newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says won't fly flags in HK after handover.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says won't fly flags in HK after handover.

text.p: Taiwan said on Monday it will not fly any flags representing its Republic of China government in Hong Kong after the British colony reverts to mainland Chinese sovereignty on July 1.

"If we are not allowed to use our national flags after the handover, all Republic of China institutions in Hong Kong ... will not use any flags with special meanings," Chang King-yuh, chairman of the Cabinet's Mainland Affairs Council, said.
He told a session of the national legislature that the decision applied only to Taiwan government offices in Hong Kong.
Private organisations were unaffected by the decision.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty on July 1 after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
China, which has viewed Taiwan as a rebel-held province since a civil war split them in 1949, has said that Taiwan can maintain its offices in Hong Kong.
But the offices must not fly the Taiwan national flag or anything signifying the island's sovereignty.

Taiwan's Education Ministry on Monday said it would hold a meeting soon to discuss a request by six ministry-subsidised Hong Kong colleges that they be allowed to stop flying Taiwan flags and to remove the phrase "Republic of China" from official documents, such as graduation certificates, after July 1.
"We would review the issue at an appropriate time," a spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone.
The institutions, including Chu Hoi College, Tak Ming College and New Asia Institute, were afraid that their connections to Taiwan would cause them problems after the handover, the reports said.
